record_type_quote: Across five conceptual replications (n = 4,559) and one highly powered, preregistered, direct replication (n = 1,235) conducted with the authors of the original paper, we observed no effect of signing first on honest reporting.

targets.authors: Shu, L. L., Mazar, N., Gino, F., Ariely, D., Bazerman, M. H.
targets.title: Signing at the beginning makes ethics salient and decreases dishonest self-reports in comparison to signing at the end.
targets.evidence_quote: Thus, in study 6, we conducted a direct replication of study 1 of the PNAS (1) manuscript (leaving out the pure control condition: no signature), given that it was the most tightly controlled laboratory experiment and it produced the largest effect size for percent of people overclaiming their performance income (d = 0.70) (1).
targets.outcome_quote: After conducting six studies that were larger and more highly powered (n = 5,794), including one direct replication of one of the two original PNAS laboratory studies, we did not replicate a sign-first effect.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict encompasses the six new experiments.

reasoning: Six fresh-sample tests target Shu et al.; other published intervention studies are background. Incidental discussion of original field data does not change the main new-data replication classification.
